name: PBB Chat
shortDescription: LAN-local community rooms, direct messages, requests, moderation, and a clear emergency handoff to Hotline.
longDescription: PBB Chat / Civitas is a Laravel community communication service for a local barangay network. It supports rooms, direct conversations, message requests, read state, badges, reports, blocks, moderation, and PBB Realtime-powered live updates.

Civitas is intentionally LAN-local and its public gateway is disabled. Emergency escalation is a handoff that returns the configured Hotline URL and context; direct incident creation, Relay synchronization, and a durable browser-offline compose queue are not confirmed.

readiness.note: Local room, direct-message, safety, moderation, Realtime, Hotline handoff, and Account integration paths are implemented.
remainingWork: Approve local message retention, moderation, backup, and purge policy.
Keep public gateway exposure disabled unless a separate security model is reviewed.
Decide whether any future selective upstream synchronization is appropriate.

problemSolved: Communities need a dependable local communication space that does not disappear with internet access, while emergency reporting remains clearly routed to the dedicated Hotline workflow.

workflowSteps.title: Enter the local community space
workflowSteps.description: A local user opens Civitas through the node LAN and joins rooms or an approved direct conversation.

workflowSteps.title: Communicate locally
workflowSteps.description: Messages persist in the local Chat database and supported live updates move through the local Realtime gateway.

workflowSteps.title: Use safety controls
workflowSteps.description: Users and moderators can report, block, mute, review, hide, or resolve supported community-safety issues.

workflowSteps.title: Hand off emergencies
workflowSteps.description: The escalation action points the user to Hotline with limited context instead of claiming direct incident creation.

localCapabilities: Rooms, direct messages, requests, safety actions, badges, and moderation are backed by the local Chat database.
The application is intended for local/LAN access with public gateway exposure disabled.
requiresLocalServices: Civitas requires its Laravel app and MySQL database.
PBB Realtime is required for confirmed live room and direct-message events; persisted records remain app-owned.
syncsWhenConnected: Account can support sign-in and app-admin provisioning when configured.
Realtime resumes supported live delivery when the local gateway is reachable.
connectivityRequired: Users need a route to the local Chat node; internet access is not a confirmed requirement.
The Hotline handoff needs the configured local Hotline URL to be reachable.
notSynchronized: No Relay synchronization of community messages or moderation data is confirmed.
No durable browser-side offline compose queue or direct Hotline incident creation is confirmed.

faqs.question: Does Civitas need the public internet?
faqs.answer: No. Civitas is designed to work on the local PBB network using its local database and live-update service.

faqs.question: Can Civitas be exposed through the public gateway?
faqs.answer: Not in the current release. Civitas should remain available only on the local network unless a separate security plan is reviewed and approved.

faqs.question: Does an escalation automatically create a Hotline incident?
faqs.answer: No. Civitas can send the user to Hotline with a small amount of helpful context, but it does not automatically create an incident.

faqs.question: Can users compose messages while disconnected from the node?
faqs.answer: This is not confirmed. Users should assume their browser must still be connected to the local Chat node to write and send messages.

faqs.question: Are community messages copied to other nodes?
faqs.answer: No. Messages, reports, blocked-user lists, and moderation records currently stay on their local node.

faqs.question: What must be approved before a live community rollout?
faqs.answer: The deployment owner must approve how long records are kept, who may moderate content, how backups and deletions work, how device sessions are handled, and what operators must do.
